props.title: Corpus Burndown — Decision Board
props.subtitle: The loop paused itself at tick 52. One convention ruling unblocks most of the board; the rest are quick calls.
props.meta: 2026-07-21 · branch Sunny-PC-burndown · all landed work double-audited

props.content: Every fix lane left on the board is gated on gold conventions, not code. The worker that was supposed to fix the "FMM ack-only leak" instead proved the gold disagrees with itself — 20 older rows vs 122 newer rows, same utterance shape, opposite expectations. Nothing here needs you to read code; each decision is a phraseology/reality call.

props.label: ticks run · 2 clean-sweep audits to close

props.content:
Four fix ticks in a row moved zero rows from fail to pass. That wasn't wasted work — each tick converted vague failures into precise, audited findings — but the pattern meant something structural. Tick 52 found it: the biggest cluster of remaining failures traces to a **gold convention conflict** the runtime cannot resolve, because the only signal that distinguishes the two conventions lives in scenario data the live system is forbidden to read.

Per the circuit-breaker rule armed two ticks earlier, the loop paused, deleted its own cron, and wrote this up instead of continuing to burn cycles.

props.title: A second real bug was found in the same trace
props.content: The row everyone blamed on the "ack-only leak" actually fails on something else: the proposal side leaves an ungoverned fix name as "SANTA CLARA VOR" while the gold-rule compiler lowercases it to "santa clara vor" — two canonicalizers with different fallback behavior, so the literal match fails. This fix is code-ready and needs no ruling (Decision 2).

props.label: DECISION 1 — THE BIG ONE
props.title: The advisory_ack convention
props.subtitle: What does the FMM receive when ATC says something that isn't an instruction?

props.content:
Model the reality: ATC says **"N17XX, radar contact."** In the air, there is nothing to comply with — the pilot acknowledges at most ("roger") and reads nothing back. But the flight manager plausibly *does* need to know radar services are established; it's situational state, not a command.

The **newer 122 rows** encode exactly that: the parser emits the intent, the readback is roger/none, and the FMM receives a **non-executable metadata command** tagged `advisory_ack`, which the fake FMM accepts via the parameterless-intent policy we landed at tick 40. The **older 20 rows** predate this convention: same utterances, but they expect the FMM to receive **nothing at all**. Same intent, same accompanying commands, opposite gold — proven with side-by-side rows below.
No runtime-legal signal distinguishes the two populations. The split correlates with scenario authoring vintage — the 20 exclusion rows look like stale gold, not a deliberate rule.

props.title: The conflict, on one utterance shape
✅ Option A — Adopt advisory_ack everywhere (recommended)
props.content:
Ruling: advisories and acknowledgments DO reach the FMM, as non-executable advisory_ack metadata.

• Matches the reality model: the FMM should know radar services are active.
• Zero runtime change for this population — the pipeline already emits these commands and the typed policy already accepts them.
• Work: re-ground the 20 stale rows (gold edits with FAA receipts, human-approved) — mostly holding_pattern_clearance and request_direct_routing.
• Keeps 122 currently-green rows green.

props.title: Option B — Exclusion principle
props.content:
Ruling: ack/advisory-class utterances never become FMM proposals.

• Requires a runtime assembly change to drop these commands.
• Requires re-grounding 122 rows the other way — 6× the gold churn.
• Regresses rows that are green today (verified against the tick-50 receipt).
• Weaker reality model: the flight manager stays blind to radar/advisory state.

props.title: Recommendation: Option A
props.content: The 122-row convention is the one the reality model, the landed typed policy, and the anti-cheat advisory route all already agree with. Your ruling here unblocks the compound FMM lane: the failing hold rows, the radar-contact compounds, and the 360_for_spacing informational cases all sit behind it.

props.label: DECISION 2
props.title: Resume shape
props.subtitle: What the loop does first when you un-pause it

props.content:
**Recommended: resume with one adjudication-prep tick, then the canonicalization fix.**

The prep tick writes the formal briefs for everything on this page (the 20-row cluster plus the 12 accumulated gold-suspects), each with FAA grounding receipts, so your rulings land as auditable gold edits instead of ad-hoc changes.

The canonicalization fix — making the proposal side and the gold-rule compiler treat ungoverned fix names the same way — is independent of every ruling and is the next genuine pass-flip candidate. It can go first if you'd rather see the board move immediately.

props.label: TL;DR
props.title: If you only rule one thing
Rule Decision 1 as Option A
props.content: Say "advisory_ack everywhere, re-ground the 20 old rows" and the loop can resume: prep tick writes the briefs, the canonicalization fix lands, and the compound FMM lane — the largest blocked cluster on the board — opens up. Everything else on this page can be ruled asynchronously.
